## Diagonal colour-dependent constant scalar frames, formal quintic, genus 2 (2026-11-04)

Log of record: `G:/My Drive/Projects/Old/refGW/hodge_vertex_quintic/logs/genus2_diag.log` (568 lines, both primes 2^89-1 and 2^61-1, 1232 s, zero FAIL lines, ends ALL DIAG CHECKS PASSED). New files (no existing module modified): `fq_diag_lib.py`, `fq_diag_report.py`, `fq_diag_solve.py`, driver `genus2_diag.py`. Scratch: `.../scratchpad/quintic_diag/mini/` (reduced pipeline test on graphs 1 and 4). Per the harness rule I did not write a write-up .md in the project folder; this report and the log are the record.

### 1. Set-up

R = R' diag(phi_i(z)), phi_i(z) = exp(a1_i z + a2_i z^3), ten independent q-constants (i = 0..4; only these orders enter at genus 2), vertex CohFT phi_i.1 at colour i, rows R phi_i^-1. fq_phi hard-codes the covariant phases zeta^{-i(2k-1)} only through its colour argument, so `fq_diag_lib.diag_frame` calls `phi_inv_coeffs(R, a1_i, a2_i, 0, Nz)` and `PhiVertexTable(R, a1_i, a2_i, 0)` per colour (`VertexTable` caches per instance, so no collision). Checked: at a1_i = zeta^-i a1, a2_i = zeta^-3i a2 the rows and vertex tables coincide with `fq_phi.phi_frame`.

Polynomial structure: the a-weight bound (weight 1 for a1, 3 for a2) of SCALAR_SCAN s.1 is colour-blind, so a coloured term is a polynomial of total a-weight <= 3 in the a's of its colours: 5 monomials (1, x, x^2, x^3, p) for one colour, 12 (1, x, y, x^2, xy, y^2, x^3, x^2y, xy^2, y^3, p, q) for two; x, y = a1 of the first/second colour of the colouring tuple, p, q = a2. Scheme: the unchanged `gsum_q.genus2_sums` at 15 random points of F_p^10 (seed p mod 1000003 + 1), the all-zero point, the covariant random point via `fq_phi.phi_frame`, and the frames F5, F4, F0 (20 sums per prime, 16-35 s each). Per coloured graph the monomial coefficients were solved from the first m points (exact F_p inverse of the m x m monomial matrix, linear combination of the NEls); the remaining 10 or 3 points are consistency checks and were reproduced exactly in N for all 115 coloured graphs (so no hidden monomial beyond the basis).

### 2. Checks in N (all PASS, both primes)

Zero point = F5 (direct frame and constant coefficient); interpolant at the covariant Hodge pattern (-zeta^-i/12, zeta^-3i/360) = F4 and at the true-class pattern (-3 zeta^-i/20, -7 zeta^-3i/2500) = F0; interpolant at the covariant random point = fq_phi frame (previous scan recovered exactly in N). Colour-shift: coef_{col+1}(mono) = zeta^{W} coef_col(mono) (W the a-weight; zeta^{-W} fails), so the 115 coloured polynomials are determined by the 23 orbit representatives. Colour-summed total: constant part = F_2 = total(F5) = total(F0), and the sum over coloured graphs of the coefficient of each non-constant global monomial is 0 exactly in N: the total is independent of all ten parameters (group property of the R-action, now colour by colour).

Zero pattern (exact in N, same at both primes): monochrome graphs 1, 2, 4: {1, x, x^2, x^3, p}; monochrome 3, 5, 6, 7: {1, x, x^2, x^3} (no a2); all 60 mixed colourings of graphs 4, 5, 7: {1, x, y, xy} only (each colour enters at most linearly: no x^2, y^2, cubics, a2); all 20 mixed colourings of the theta graph 6: {1} (no a-dependence at all). 51 global monomials occur (none with three colours).

### 3. Valuation bookkeeping (Cf, s = 1/L, u = s^5)

Exact (from the L-powers of the numerator keys, all orders): the exponent classes of the Cf image of an a-weight-W coefficient are {-W mod 5} = {0}, {4}, {3}, {2} for W = 0..3, and the maximal L-degrees are 10, 6, 2, -2, so val >= -10, -6, -2, +2 exactly; series version to O(s^80): val = -10 for all 115 constants, min valuations -6, -2, 2 attained. Hence the polar part of a coloured term is
const_-10 s^-10 + const_-5 s^-5 + Sum_c a1_c (X_c,-6 s^-6 + X_c,-1 s^-1) + Sum_{c<=c'} a1_c a1_c' (Q_cc',-2 s^-2),
the a2's never polar, and (distinct classes) a term is a u-series iff its weight-1, weight-2 and weight-3 parts vanish separately.

### 4. Tables (log section (5); residues and Q(zeta) coordinates at 2^89-1, residues at 2^61-1)

Constants are the point-frame values of SCALAR_SCAN s.3 (e.g. vertex 1807/15360000, -7/40000). Monochrome representatives have the covariant entries (x s^-6, x s^-1, x^2 s^-2) = (T1_-6, T1_-1, T2_-2) of the old table, e.g. graph 2: -343/64000, 19/1600, 89/1920; graph 4 (0,0): -73/256000, 1/1500, 71/7680. Mixed colourings split the old T1, T2 into colour-resolved pieces, e.g. graph 4 at (0,1): x s^-6 = -(1 + 2z + 2z^2 + z^3)/4000, y s^-6 = (z + 2z^2 + z^3)/4000, x s^-1 = 1/6000 + z/1500 + z^2/2000 + z^3/4000, y s^-1 = 1/6000 - z/3000 - z^2/2000 - z^3/4000, xy s^-2 = 1/200 + 3z/200 + z^2/200 (identical to the xy entry of the dumbbell 7 at (0,1)); graph 4 at (0,2): x s^-6 = 1/4000 + z/4000 + z^3/2000, y s^-6 = -(2 + z + z^2 + 2z^3)/4000, xy s^-2 = -z/200 + z^2/100 - z^3/200; graph 5 at (0,1): x s^-6 = (1 + 2z + 2z^2 + z^3)/2000, y s^-6 = (1 + 3z + z^2)/2000, x s^-1 = -1/3000 - z/750 - z^2/1000 - z^3/2000, y s^-1 = -(17 + 41z + 17z^2)/10000, xy s^-2 = -(1 + 3z + z^2)/100; graph 7 at (0,1): x s^-6 = -1/2000 + (z^2 + z^3)/4000, y s^-6 = -(1 + 3z + z^2)/4000, x s^-1 = 3/2500 - 17(z^2 + z^3)/20000, y s^-1 = (17 + 41z + 17z^2)/20000; mixed theta: constants only. Check: x + zeta^-1 y at (0,1) of graph 4 gives -(z^2 + z^3)/4000 = the old T1_-6. The full 23-row table with all 179 polar entries (Q(zeta) coordinates reconstructed from the Galois conjugates col -> m col, back-substitution verified) and the compact 115-row residue table are in the log; the covariant specialisation reproduces all 115 leading coefficients (T0_-10, T1_-6, T2_-2, T3_2, T4_2) parsed from genus2_scalar.log at each prime. Leading weight-3 coefficients at s^2 (never polar): vertex x^3 -131/3456, p 23/1152; graph 2: -1/288, -1/48; 3: 1/8, 0; 4 (0,0): -397/3456, 1/1152; 5: 23/96, 0; 6: -1/12, 0; 7: -1/8, 0; all mixed colourings 0.

### 5. Solves (identical at both primes)

FULL system (all negative powers of s of the 110 coloured edge graphs = 0): the s^-10 and s^-5 coefficients are the a-independent constants, non-zero for 110 of 110 (both orders). Inconsistent: no choice of the ten constants touches them, exactly as the bookkeeping predicts.

WEAK system (a-dependent polar coefficients only): 220 linear forms in (a1_0..a1_4) from s^-6 and s^-1 (180 non-zero; the 40 zero ones are the mixed theta colourings), 90 quadratic forms from s^-2. Gaussian elimination: rank 5, RREF = {a1_0 = a1_1 = a1_2 = a1_3 = a1_4 = 0}; the rank is already 5 from the s^-6 forms alone, from the s^-1 forms alone, from the 30 monochrome edge graphs alone, from the 80 mixed colourings alone, and from any single edge graph 2..7 with all its colourings. Kernel dimension 5 = the five a2_i, which no polar coefficient involves. The quadratics vanish identically on the kernel. Exact solution set: a1_i = 0 for all i, a2_i arbitrary (dimension 5). So colour dependence buys nothing: the weak solution set is the same as for the covariant scalar, now per colour.

u-series statement (all orders to O(s^80)): the 2780 non-zero weight-1 series coefficients (class 4) have rank 5 in the a1's; given a1 = 0 the 240 non-zero p, q series coefficients (class 2) have rank 5 in the a2's (160 and rank 5 from edge graphs alone: monochrome graphs 2 and 4 carry a2 terms). Every coloured term is a u-series only in the point frame, all ten constants zero. The frames F4 and F0 are not.

### 6. Cross-prime and caveats

179 table entries: Q(zeta) coordinates reconstructed at 2^89-1 (0 failures, bound 10^10), reduced mod 2^61-1, equal the 2^61-1 residues; at 2^61-1 the two known entries 1807/15360000 and -31/15360000 exceed the ratrec bound 10737418 (residues 1393615335851750081, 1550751631410234689, compared by residue). Zero patterns, valuations, counts, ranks, pivots, kernel dimension and solution set identical at both primes. Timings: 715 s at 2^89-1 (20 sums of 16-35 s, 1135 Cf substitutions 39 s), 517 s at 2^61-1.

Caveats: genus 2 only (a3 and higher never enter); exact finite data at two primes, AI-checked only; the bilinear structure of mixed colourings is an observed exact fact in N, not derived here (the naive weight count allows x^2 through the edge's extra order, so there are cancellations); the per-graph entries beyond their consistency with the previous table were not independently re-derived. No bugs found in the existing modules; `py -I` needs the usual `sys.path` insertion (done in fq_diag_lib).

The weak-system rank is 5 from any single edge graph (2..7) with all its colourings, and from s^-6 or s^-1 alone: the conclusion a1 = 0 is heavily overdetermined
